who: Historian of modern Japan at the University of Michigan, PhD Chicago 1990.

evidence.says: Michigan retirement memoir identifies the modern Japanese historian, appointed in 1995 and retiring in December 2018, with a Chicago PhD in 1990.
LC identifies Leslie Pincus, with the fuller name Leslie Beth Pincus, from The allure of difference (1989).
Chicago departmental history, p. 55, lists Leslie B. Pincus and The Allure of Difference: Iki No Kozo and the Construction of the Japanese Spirit among its dissertations.

notes: The LC dissertation, Chicago training and Japanese intellectual-history field align. The dissertation is listed under 1989; Michigan gives the degree year as 1990.

who: Historian of British politics and journalism at Simon Fraser University, formerly at Waterloo, PhD Oxford.

evidence.says: Official biography identifies the SFU emeritus history professor, previously a Waterloo history professor and associate dean, with an Oxford doctorate and publications on British politics and journalism.
The Canadian Historical Association winter 2009 bulletin reports John Stubbs retiring from the Simon Fraser history department.
LC identifies John O. Stubbs from Mackenzie King (1977); its source note describes him as associate chairman of history at Waterloo.

notes: The Waterloo appointment links the LC candidate to the SFU professor; Oxford education and the supervision period also agree.

who: Professor of Byzantine history at Notre Dame since 2015, PhD Vienna 1999.

evidence.says: CV gives a Vienna doctorate in Byzantine studies in 1999 and Notre Dame appointments from 2015 onward; publications include Quellenkritische Untersuchungen zu den ägyptischen Kapitulationsverträgen der Jahre 640–646 (2000).
LC authorizes Alexander Daniel Beihammer from that same 2000 monograph and also records the usage Alexander Beihammer.

notes: Exact shared publication connects the name forms; institution, period, field and doctoral institution agree.

who: Cultural historian of modern Korea at the University of Wisconsin–Madison, PhD Columbia.

evidence.says: Faculty profile gives Columbia PhD, modern Korean cultural-history specialization, and authorship of Youth for Nation: Culture and Protest in Cold War South Korea (2017).
The 2018 PhD ceremony page explicitly names Charles Kim as Hye Eun Choi’s advisor.
LC identifies Charles R. Kim from Youth for nation (2017).

notes: The shared book identifies the Charles R. Kim authority as the Wisconsin supervisor; the department confirms a listed advisee.

who: Historian of American women and culture at Case Western Reserve University, PhD William & Mary.

evidence.says: Case faculty profile identifies the history professor and author of Performing Menken: Adah Isaacs Menken and the Birth of American Celebrity (2003).
The graduate handbook lists Renée Sentilles as a history professor with a William & Mary PhD, specializing in women’s history, American history and American studies.
LC authorizes Renée M. Sentilles from Performing Menken (2003).

notes: Exact shared book establishes the authority match; affiliation, field and doctoral institution agree.

who: Historian of Egypt and the Middle East at the University of Maryland during the 1960s.

evidence.says: A 1961 American Historical Review contribution identifies Helen Anne B. Rivlin with the University of Maryland.
Maryland State Archives names Helen Anne B. Rivlin as professor of history at the University of Maryland.
LC authorizes Helen Anne B. Rivlin from The agricultural policy of Muhammad Ali in Egypt (1961).

notes: The fuller name is documented at Maryland in the relevant period, and the authority’s Egypt specialization fits the supervisor’s field.

who: History supervisor at Loyola University Chicago in the 1950s.

evidence.says: Loyola’s institutional-history exhibit credits Joseph Roubik with an unpublished history of the university.
LC identifies J. R. (Joseph R.) Roubik through Review of materials processing literature (1971), whose cover describes a project engineer in research and development at Kearney & Trecker, Milwaukee.

notes: The sole candidate is a materials-processing engineer, a different professional identity from the Loyola historian.

who: Drew historian of modern German intellectual history, teaching there 1965–1996, PhD European history Northwestern 1963.

evidence.says: The newspaper obituary identifies John Thomas von der Heide, his Northwestern European-history doctorate in 1963, and his Drew teaching from 1965 to retirement in 1996.
Jürgen Heide is identified from Controversies in the treatment of lung cancer, with a radiooncology and radiotherapy affiliation in Berlin.
J. von der Heide is identified from Perth 70 (1976), with Hamburg Observatory affiliation.
J. van der Heide is identified from a 1989 nutrient-management work, affiliated with the Institute for Soil Fertility in Haren.
J. ter (Jack) Heide is identified from Kort begrip van Romeins recht (1967), a work on Roman law.

notes: All four proposed authorities concern other scholars in different fields; none identifies the Drew historian.
